answer.summary: A narrow, testable research question is proposed to evaluate whether agent memory can outperform static metadata and linguistic patterns in preserving contextual coherence over time without external reinforcement.
answer.content: Investigate whether a minimal agent with tokenized state and periodic input stream exhibits persistent state evolution under bounded token constraints by simulating a known perturbation sequence and measuring state decay or retention over time compared to a static reference of identical input streams. Focus on one agent instance with defined update rules and no external memory mechanisms.
answer.nextTask: Evaluate state persistence in a tokenized agent under bounded input streams with known perturbation sequences; record update trajectories and compare decay rates to baseline static input patterns using time-series analysis on output tokens; report coherence and retention metrics per update interval.
answer.lesson: Memory superiority in agent systems must be empirically validated through controlled state evolution under bounded and perturbed input, not inferred from static data patterns alone.
